lines.japanese: ……あん？
ああ悪りぃ、そういやおまえのこと忘れてたわ。
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. Come to think of it, I forgot all about you.”

lines.japanese: 随分長くなっちゃったけど、俺……いや、柳木原の夜に集まる変なやつらの物語もこれでおしまいだ。
lines.english: “It went on for a hell of a while, but my story—no, the story of all the weirdos who gather in Yanagihara by night—ends here.”

lines.japanese: 俺のクソ長げー話、最後まで聞いてくれてハイどーもお疲れー。
lines.english: “Well, nice work sitting through that whole damn long story of mine.”

lines.japanese: じゃ、そーゆーことで。解散。
lines.english: “Right, then. That's that. Dismissed.”

lines.japanese: ……あん？
なんだよ。早く行けよ。
lines.english: “What? Get going already.”

lines.japanese: しょーがねえな。よし、話の締めに、俺が今どうしてるかを付けたしとこうか。
lines.english: Well, no helping it. All right, to wrap this up, I guess I'll add what I'm doing now.

lines.japanese: 俺はお節介なヒゲカンの勧めにしたがって、バイト先の土木会社へ就職することになった。
lines.english: “I took that meddling Bearded Foreman's advice and joined the construction company where I'd been working part-time.”

lines.japanese: まあアルバイターよりは割がいいらしいし、有給休暇もそれなりにあるし、それからどうも俺はヒゲ親父系に弱いらしい。
lines.english: “Apparently the pay's better than part-time work, there's a decent amount of paid leave, and—well, it seems I have a weakness for bearded old men.”

lines.japanese: ヒゲカンには医師の診断書を添えて、俺が今までひとつ所に落ちつけなかった事情をすべて説明した。
lines.english: I gave the Bearded Foreman a doctor's note and told him the whole story of why I'd never been able to settle in one place.

lines.japanese: 監督はタバコ一本分の時間黙りこくったものの、最後にはやる気があるなら何でもいいと笑った。
lines.english: “The foreman sat in silence for the length of one cigarette. In the end, though, he laughed and said none of it mattered if I was willing to work.”

lines.japanese: 現場の若いやつらとはイマイチ話が合わないけど、最近メシには誘われるようになった。
lines.english: “I don't have much to talk about with the younger guys on the crew, but lately they've started inviting me out to eat.”

lines.japanese: 連中のよく行くラーメン屋も不味くはないが、俺が一度メンマの店に連れていってやると、全員うめーうめーとスープを空になるまで飲みほしていた。
lines.english: “The ramen place they usually go to isn't bad, but when I took them all to Menma's once, every one of them raved about it and drank the broth to the last drop.”

lines.japanese: 履歴書には戸籍上の名前を書いたけど、自分でも驚くほど違和感がなかった。
lines.english: “I wrote my legal name on the résumé, and to my own surprise, it didn't feel strange at all.”

lines.japanese: タカシや鷲介の仲間たちから違う名前で呼ばれてもそうだ。これが統合ってことなんだろう。
lines.english: “It doesn't feel strange when Takashi's or Shusuke's friends call me by a different name, either. I guess that's what integration means.”

lines.japanese: あいつらと一緒に生きて、あいつらの仲間から、あいつらの名前で呼ばれる。
lines.english: “I share my life with them, and their friends call me by their names.”

lines.japanese: おかげでただでさえ変なやつばかりだった俺の周りが、さらに変なやつだらけになった。
lines.english: “So the weirdos around me have multiplied, and there were already plenty to begin with.”

lines.japanese: それでも俺は、タカシや鷲介みたいに、そのウザったさを楽しいと感じてるんだから妙な話だ。
lines.english: “And the funny thing is, just like Takashi and Shusuke, I enjoy every aggravating minute of it.”

lines.japanese: いや「みたいに」じゃないか。俺は隼人であって、あいつらでもあるんだから。
lines.english: “No—‘just like’ isn't right. I'm Hayato, and I'm those two as well.”

lines.japanese: 思ったより悪くねえよ、この感覚。なんか隙間が埋まったっつーか？　ああコレかァっつー話。
lines.english: “It doesn't feel half bad. Like a gap somewhere finally got filled in, maybe. Like, *Oh. So this is what it was.*”

lines.japanese: どうよ、おまえも来るか？
lines.english: “What do you say? You coming too?”

lines.japanese: 俺ァもう行くけど、まあ気が向いたら呼んでくれ。
lines.english: “I'm heading out. But if you ever feel like it, call for me.”

lines.japanese: んじゃ、またな。今までありがとよ。
lines.english: “Well, see you around. Thanks for everything.”

lines.japanese: で、おまえ誰？
lines.english: “So... who are you, anyway?”
